items.title: Skift Global Forum Preview: Amadeus’s President of Travel on Why the Traveler, Not the Platform, Should Hold the Controls
items.summary: Decius Valmorbida thinks the industry competes too hard on closed ecosystems and cooperates too little on the plumbing. His bet: open, shared foundations grow the pie for everyone. We'll test whether rivals actually build them together at Skift Global Forum this September.

items.title: Travel Execs Push Trump for 100 Million+ International Visitors by 2030
items.summary: The meeting comes on the heels of the World Cup tournament and follows four consecutive months of inbound travel declines.

items.title: Uber to Lay Off 3,300 Employees, Reducing Management Jobs by 20%
items.summary: Uber's reorganization doesn't directly impact its product portfolio, according to the company, but its attention is focused on core businesses.

items.title: Southwest to Launch ‘at Least’ 11 Airport Lounges in Chase Partnership
items.summary: Lounges are the latest step in Southwest’s rapid transformation from a low-cost domestic carrier to a full-service operator.

items.title: Virgin’s New International Trains Could Cut Emissions, Fares — and Fuel Its Loyalty Program
items.summary: Increased competition on the track connecting the UK and continental Europe could be a win for the environment if it pulls travelers off planes, but prices need to be lower. Virgin has another incentive in mind: loyalty points.

items.title: Ryanair Pulls Winter Capacity and Warns Rivals May Struggle to Survive
items.summary: Ryanair has a fuel hedge most airlines would envy, and it's still cutting unprofitable winter flights. Its more exposed rivals should be nervous.

items.title: The Economics of Flight Search, Post-Google
items.summary: Skyscanner, Kiwi.com, and Wego built different businesses around the same problem: helping people find flights. Their latest private company filings show what that business is worth after Google — and what AI may change next.

items.title: Saudi Tourism Names New CEO As Kingdom Pulls Back On Vision 2030 Spending
items.summary: Ageel Alshaibani inherits a goal of drawing 150 million tourists — a tough ask now that the Public Investment Fund is pulling back on the giga projects built to draw them.
